newsitem.title: USA: Illinois fieldwork last week slowed by rainfall.
newsitem.headline: Illinois fieldwork last week slowed by rainfall.

text.p: Scattered rainfall last week slowed fieldwork in Illinois and caused concern for the wheat growing region in the south which had local flooding, according to the Illinois Agricultural Statistics Service.
Days suitable for fieldwork from June 7-13 had a state avrerage of 3.0 days, with the most in the northwest at 4.6 and slowest in the southeast at 1.4.
Topsoil moisture as of Friday was six percent short, 58 percent adequate and 36 percent surplus. In southeast Illinois, topsoil moisture was 11 percent adequate and 89 percent surplus.
Corn crop conditions as of Friday were 12 percent excellent, 60 percent good, 24 percent fair, three percent poor and one percent very poor.
Soybeans were rated seven percent excellent, 60 percent good, 28 percent fair and five percent poor.

As of Sunday, wheat was ripe on less than one percent of the acreage, compared with two percent a year ago and six percent for the five year average. 27 percent of the crop was turning yellow, compared with 29 percent last year and 48 percent for the average.
Winter wheat was eight percent excellent, 64 percent good, 23 percent fair and five percent poor, down slightly from the previous week.
Oats were 15 percent excellent, 66 percent good, 18 percent fair and one percent poor.
Pasture conditions were nine percent excellent, 64 percent good, 23 percent fair, three percent poor and one percent very poor.
